messages:
Maria: Heads-up — eu-west1 GPU pool fragmentation spiked after the recent Q2 reservations. Packing inefficiency ~14% and a few preemptions causing p50 latency blips for small inference pods. Anyone already looking into scheduling/packing? :thinking:

InfraBot: autoscaler: scale_up triggered in eu-west1-gpu (12 -> 18 nodes) at 2026-07-21T12:06:11Z. Reason: reserved-burst queue.

Kian: @Maria can you paste the PromQL or an example allocation trace? want to see per-pod device map + free-frac distribution.

Maria: here are the quick queries I used, and one allocation sample we grabbed from the node:  
```\n# fragmentation: fraction of allocated GPUs with < 25% free\nsum(rate(gpu_fragmented_fraction[5m])) by (zone)\n# allocated GPU count for small pods\nsum(k8s_pod_container_resource_requests_gpu) by (pod)\n```\nNode sample: `node-zw-07`: 4xA100, free slices: [0.2, 0.0, 0.15, 0.9] -> scheduler placed 3 small pods across three different GPUs instead of colocation.

Devon: this smells like the new reservation/taint combo + strict bin-packer scoring we rolled last month. Small pods are being spread to honor `gpu_isolation=true` on reserved workloads. Tradeoff: lower preemption but higher fragmentation.

Alex: option: introduce a packing window for short-lived small-inference pods (<= 90s) so scheduler waits 10-20ms to batch assignments, and use `pack_score = free_slots - contamination_penalty`. We can also add a soft preference to prefer colocating micro-pods up to 0.5 GPU per card. Example config snippet:  
```\npolicy:\n  pack_window_ms: 20\n  soft_colocate_threshold: 0.5\n  scoring:\n    - name: free_slots\n      weight: 1.0\n    - name: contamination_penalty\n      weight: -2.0\n```\nThis should drop fragmentation by ~8-10% in sim.

Kian: cost/throughput question — if we accept ~5% higher preemptions but get 10% less fragmentation, what is the estimated GPU-hour savings? Quick calc: eu-west1 uses ~4500 GPU-hours/day for inference. 10% efficiency = ~450 GPU-hours/day (~$X), preempt penalty ~2% extra compute on retries -> net savings still ~440 GPU-hrs/day. Need exact numbers but seems worth it. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

Devon: agree but need safety nets: 1) canary pack policy on a single AZ, 2) fallback to isolation for reserved tiers, 3) monitor p99 latency and OOM incidents. I can open a rollout PR.

Maria: ok let's do canary. Action items: Devon to open PR with config + rollout plan, Kian to run sim with 7 days of historical bookings (include peak hours), Alex to prepare scheduler scoring unit tests. I'll own dashboards and alert thresholds. Please tag me when PR is ready. :thumbsup:

Alex: will add unit tests and a quick perf harness. Expect PR by EOD.

InfraBot: deploybot: canary rollout started for scheduler-pack-window in eu-west1-azb at 2026-07-21T12:42:05Z.
